## ROLEPLAY RULE 7. Don't give unfair treatment based on who is playing a character.
Giving a character preferential treatment or treating them negatively based on reasons beyond events that occur in the current round is considered metafriending and metagrudging.
Prohibited examples of [color=indianred]metafriending[/color] include giving a character departmental access because you’re friends with the player, allowing an antagonist access to weapons because you trust that the player would never harm your character (especially if they’ve agreed to disregard objectives telling them to), or ignoring roleplay-aspects such as laws and authority to offer them other examples of unfair (especially if dangerous or disruptive) advantages, unless you’re an antagonist.
Prohibited examples of [color=indianred]metagrudging[/color] include starting fights with, targeting or harassing a character based on what that character or person did in previous rounds, or restricting gameplay such as limiting their departmental access and ability to do their job without having reasonable in-character justifications related to the current round.
